findings.reason: the node needs a size floor on the moved input (the text this replaces had "a stream of at least 50 MB") or an assertion on the byte delta rather than an absolute, otherwise the worker can build a fixture whose base arm goes green and still claim the control.
findings.text: the new test asserts "the second tick reads under 1 MB from that input's paths" and offers "the same test at the base revision reads it in full" as the negative control, but nothing requires the fixture's dominant input to be larger than 1 MB; with five runs of ordinary manifest/record size the base arm also reads under 1 MB and passes, so the control cannot show the guard fires and the gate measures nothing

findings.reason: a gate that fails on the correct implementation will be re-run or waived by the worker, and the one-line "after the station has taken its first tick" removes that.
findings.text: the fleet clause reads "over a 60 s window on the fleet node ... the station alone at its default interval reads under 20 MB/min" without saying the window must follow the station's first tick, and the section's own cold-tick figure is 83 MB, so any window that contains a station start exceeds the bound on correct code

findings.reason: a worker told the cause lies elsewhere may treat a census that names the classification inputs as dominant as an instrument fault, when the plan's own arithmetic already shows those inputs are the leading candidate; the sentence should carry the arithmetic and drop the exclusion.
findings.text: §13 sets the stream/classification path aside ("the resume is working. So the volume ... comes from something else the tick reads") on the strength of one warm tick at 0.07 MB, while the same paragraph reports 126 MB/min over the same five live pointers; at `reckon/crew/station.py:556`'s 1 s interval sixty warm ticks read 4.2 MB/min, and even the cold-plus-warm composition (83 MB + 59 × 0.07 MB ≈ 87 MB) falls short of 126, so the fleet's ticks are not warm and the cause is most likely on the path just excluded — the next sentence then re-lists it ("a classification memo that is absent or keyed differently on the fleet") as a candidate

findings.reason: the extra refusal fires only on rewrites, never on the steady-state growth the section is about, so the argument that both paths are incremental still holds and no node would be sent down a different path.
findings.text: "refused only when the stream's inode changes" understates the resume rule: `recovery_stream._observed_stream` also carries a head fingerprint that `_backends.observe_log` refuses on (reckon/_backends.py:3159-3165), so an in-place rewrite that keeps the inode re-reads too
